changes: - Lots of initial work towards simply setting up a hexagonal grid. I've always wanted to make a hex grid, but never actually done it.
- The hex grid renders, and fills available space based on how much space is available on the screen,

- Allowed the player to pan the camera around the screen, and did a lot of work to try and sell the illusion that the space is infinite. Right now, new cells are created as you pan the camera around, but old cells that are inactive are still kept. I need to remove those.

- I'm making it so that the game renders fake tiles that aren't persistent until the tile is actually involved in the simulation. Creating untouched tiles on the fly seems faster than remembering every tile that's ever been created.
- Now when the game first loads, you spawn centered at (0, 0, 0)
- Wrote the logic for finding which hex your mouse is on.
- Added the window where the components like mechanisms and reagents will go.
- Added a neat collapsing effect where that window can be hidden or shown.
- Created an image for the first atom, Fire.
- The computer can now render an atom in the correct location
- Created some of the basics for displaying a molecule that contains two bonded atoms.
- The game can now correctly rotate molecules around a point, but it can only do it in whole integer amounts right now.

- The game can now render molecules with a non-integer rotation. The atoms it draws this way are not actually stored as being where they claim to be, and only rendered there. I will need to do a lot of math again to determine their locations in the game logic for collision checks and stuff.
- Now components can be offset in non-integer amounts for smooth translations.
- Added a way for me to see the coordinates of any tile I want. It's getting hard to remember which is which.
- Added a prototype kind of arm, that can rotate the same way molecules can. Currently it can't actually affect molecules by itself, but it's there.
- Added the different categories of thing you can drag onto the grid from the left panel. Right now the only thing you can use is pistons.
- You can now place things onto the grid. Right now the only thing you can place is pistons.
- Placing something onto the grid is prevented if you try to place something on top of something else.
- Starting to work on allowing some programming from the player. I set up som eof the stuff that needs to go on the bottom panel.
- Placing a new arm onto the page now creates a corresponding row in the programming pane that, eventually, I hope to be able to drag and drop commands onto. I even made it make a nice rainbow.
- Arms now display the number of the corresponding program on their base.
- You can now drag and drop instructions onto the programs you create.
- You can now move previously placed instructions around.
- Finally starting to work on simulating the game. Right now you can tell your arms to rotate right and left. That's it.
- Empty instructions are removed from the end of your programs.
- You can now press the play button and it will play your program.

- You can now stop the playback, and it will reset everything back to how it was before you pressed play. This is done through a very hacky method: The computer just creates a copy of the level and then animates that.
- Now, when the simulation starts and every tick afterward, if the game is able, it places molecules on any reagents you've placed.
- Added the grab, drop, extend, retract, pivot clockwise, and pivot counterclockwise instructions.
- The collision detection is more accurate now and takes into account where a molecule is even while it's in the middle of an animation.
- If two atoms collide during a simulation, the simulation stops.
- If you place a molecule on a product, and that molecule fits, the molecule disappears.
- Programs now loop! And they even allow you to have empty space at the beginning, and properly calculate their periods! (as long as you don't use a period override. haven't done that yet.)
- Now when you pick up an instruction, you can see it as a tooltip following your mouse.
- You can finally click and drag components around after placing them.
- You can now click and drag products and reagents onto the screen like you can arms!
- Reagents now properly show the molecules they make while the simulation isn't running.
- You can now rotate components around after placing them!
- You can now change the initial length of arms!
- Starting to work on rendering glyphs. They seem like they'll be very hard to work with so far.
- The game can now render the glyph of bonding, but it doesn't have functionality yet.
- The game can now detect which atoms are sitting on top of the inputs of a glyph.
- The bonder glyph works now.
- Now, moving molecules in impossible ways is detected by the simulation and prevented.
- The game only shows you a component's rotation handle if your mouse is close enough.
- Pretty sure the game's engine supports any playback speed you want
- You can now place tracks, but they don't work yet.
- You can now click and drag to place more tracks.
- Tracks figure out which image that the need to use to appear connected, but don't currently rotate correctly to show it.
- Huge improvement to how the computer determines which hexagon your mouse is hovering over.
- Tracks can loop and display their tracks correctly when they do.

- Making the tracks look good was a huge headache and I also didn't make them look very good. At some point I'll come through and try making them nicer, but unfortunately I don't know how to make the images look good without shaders that I am trying to avoid using.
